source_evidence: If you die before you start receiving payments, the person you name as your beneficiary receives at least the current value of the annuity, perhaps more.
answer: An annuity death benefit is money paid to a named beneficiary when the annuity owner dies. If the owner dies before income payments begin, the beneficiary receives at least the annuity’s current value, and the benefit may be higher. The amount and rules can depend on the contract, so review how the benefit is calculated during both the accumulation and payout phases.
